content.value_statement: Agents lose useful context when sessions end or facts change over time. This skill helps design persistent memory with vectors, graphs, and temporal retrieval.
actual_capabilities: Explains layered memory architecture from working memory to permanent storage.
Compares vector stores, knowledge graphs, temporal knowledge graphs, and summarization.
Provides patterns for file-system memory, vector RAG, graph memory, and temporal graphs.
Includes Python reference implementations for vector search, graph storage, and temporal querying.
Guides retrieval patterns for semantic, entity-based, and time-based memory access.
Describes consolidation triggers for merging, archiving, and deleting outdated memories.
limitations: The examples are educational and are not production-ready storage services.
The sample vector store uses demonstration embeddings, not a real embedding model.
The skill does not implement authentication, access controls, or retention policy.
Performance claims should be validated against your own data and infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Build Persistent Agent Memory
use_cases.description: Design memory layers for agents that need continuity across sessions and reliable recall.

use_cases.title: Model Customer and Entity History
use_cases.description: Choose graph or temporal storage when products, users, accounts, or preferences change over time.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Memory Architecture Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Compare vector retrieval, graph traversal, temporal queries, latency, and accuracy for a new system.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Memory Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the memory-systems skill to choose a memory pattern for my agent. The agent must [goal], remember [data], and answer [queries].

prompt_templates.title: Design Layered Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a layered memory architecture for [agent]. Include working memory, short-term memory, long-term memory, entity memory, and temporal memory where useful.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Temporal Retrieval
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the memory-systems skill to design temporal retrieval for [entities] and [facts]. Include validity periods, query patterns, and consolidation rules.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this memory system design for gaps in retrieval quality, privacy, consolidation, scaling, and failure handling: [design].

output_examples.input: I need memory for a support agent that remembers customer preferences.
output_examples.output: Recommended architecture: session memory for active cases, entity memory for customers, and temporal facts for preference changes.

output_examples.input: The agent must answer what a user knew last month.
output_examples.output: Use temporal relationships with validity periods. Retrieve facts valid at the requested time before adding them to context.

output_examples.input: Our vector memory misses relationships between customers and products.
output_examples.output: Move relationship-heavy facts into a property graph. Keep vector search for broad semantic recall and unstructured notes.

best_practices: Start with query requirements before choosing a storage pattern.
Store source, timestamp, confidence, and validity period with important facts.
Add privacy, retention, deletion, and access controls before storing long-term personal data.
anti_patterns: Treating vector similarity search as complete memory when relationships matter.
Storing every interaction forever without consolidation or retention limits.
Using demo memory code as production storage without durability, indexing, and access control.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design agent memory systems that preserve state, entities, relationships, and temporal facts across sessions.

faq.question: Does it include a production database integration?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and educational Python examples for memory system design.

faq.question: Can it help choose between vector RAG and knowledge graphs?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when semantic retrieval is enough and when relationship traversal or temporal queries are needed.

faq.question: Does the skill store user data by itself?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes designs and examples. Your application decides where and how data is stored.

faq.question: How should personal data be handled?
faq.answer: Use consent, retention limits, deletion workflows, encryption, and access controls before storing long-term personal data.

faq.question: Is the sample implementation production-ready?
faq.answer: No. It is a reference for learning. Replace demo embeddings and in-memory stores before production use.
